evals.prompt: I want a card that shows the user's Jio account balance. It should have the account number, the balance amount in big text, and a 'Recharge' button. We're on the Finance vertical.
evals.expected_output: A structured Design Brief with surface context, component specs, colour intent, spacing, states, and flags for unconfirmed values
assertions: Output includes a surface context section explaining card-on-surface pairing rule
Recharge button is specified as pill-shaped (rounded-full)
Balance amount uses a headline type token (not a raw px value)
Loading state specifies skeleton shimmer, not a spinner
A 🚩 flag is raised for the unconfirmed Finance vertical action colour

evals.prompt: Can you check if the home screen follows our design system? It has a spinner while loading, the CTA button has slightly rounded corners (not fully pill-shaped), and there's a gradient on the hero banner.
evals.expected_output: A compliance review with clear PASS/FAIL for each item, and plain-language instructions on how to fix each failure
assertions: Spinner is marked as FAIL with a clear fix (skeleton shimmer)
Button corners are marked as FAIL with the correct fix (rounded-full / pill shape)
Gradient is marked as FAIL with the correct fix (flat colour only)
Output is understandable to a non-technical reader
No code syntax or class names leak into the plain-language summary

evals.prompt: Hey, can I add a drop shadow to make our cards look more premium? Also can I use a different font for the headline to make it feel more unique?
evals.expected_output: Clear plain-language answers explaining why both are not allowed, with an alternative suggestion for each
assertions: Shadow is correctly refused with an explanation of the alternative (surface contrast)
Font change is correctly refused with explanation (JioType is fixed)
An alternative is offered for each request (spacing for premium feel, Black weight for distinctive headlines)
Answer uses no code or class names — entirely plain language
